title: add vpc control plane terraform multi-az peering endpoints dns and upgrade hooks
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds Terraform modules for multi-AZ private control plane provisioning (subnets, interface endpoints, peering, DNS) and installer upgrade/rollback hooks. Backwards compatible with existing single-AZ configs.
description:
Context: Customers deploying Redwood Private across multiple availability zones require stable control-plane networking: per-AZ subnets, interface endpoints for control-plane services, cross-account VPC peering for management plane, and Route53 private hosted zone delegation. The existing single-AZ Terraform module and installer hooks didn't cover multi-AZ peering and graceful upgrades.

What this PR does (summary): Adds a new version of the vpc_control_plane Terraform module with multi-AZ support (public/private subnets per-AZ), configurable interface endpoints for S3/STS/ECR, automated cross-VPC peering and route propagation, and Route53 private hosted zone associations. Adds Helm/installer upgrade and rollback hooks to ensure DNS records and peering are created before the control-plane starts and cleaned up on rollback. Includes integration tests and documentation updates.

Motivation: Without coordinated provisioning of peering and DNS, control-plane instances in private deployments can fail to register or route to shared services during upgrades or scale events. This change reduces downtime risk during upgrades and enables multi-AZ resilience.

Checklist:
- [x] Terraform module: multi-az subnets, interface endpoints, peering, route tables
- [x] Installer hooks: pre-upgrade create-peering/check-dns, post-upgrade patch, rollback cleanup
- [x] Helm values updated to support multi-az control-plane topology
- [x] Integration tests for peering + DNS association (mocked AWS)
- [x] Docs: private-deploy multi-az guide and troubleshooting

Backward compatibility notes: The module preserves previous top-level variables and defaults for single-AZ deployments. Default behavior when multi_az_enabled=false is unchanged. The installer hooks are opt-in via a helm value (installer.upgradeHooks.enabled).

Operational notes:
- This introduces IAM permissions required for peering and route table modifications; see docs/permissions.md.
- Peering is created with explicit route table propagation; in cross-account setups an operator must accept peering if auto-accept=false.
- We added a readiness probe in the installer that waits for private hosted zone association to propagate (TTL-aware).

Follow-ups: audit logging for peering acceptance flow (ENG-4980), deeper e2e with real AWS accounts (ENG-4821).
